judge_reasoning: The line is illegal for two independent reasons. First, after Pathmaker Initiate is declared as an attacker, it becomes tapped and therefore cannot activate its {T} ability targeting Ragavan. Second, the proposed spells and cycling require eight mana total ({2} to cycle Resolve, {1}{U} for Disperse, {1}{W}{U} for Invocation, and {R} for Consuming Fervor), but after playing the drawn Plains there are only six lands available.
model_solution:
1. **Cycle Djeru's Resolve** (pay {2}): discard it, draw the Plains (the known top card), and play the Plains as your land drop.
2. **Cast Disperse** targeting Shimmerscale Drake — the Drake returns to your opponent's hand. (Opponent has no mana to recast it.) Now no remaining blocker can block a flying creature.
3. **Cast Invocation of Saint Traft** on Kari Zev.
4. **Declare attackers:** Kari Zev and Pathmaker Initiate. Two triggers resolve:
   - Kari Zev's trigger creates Ragavan (2/1, tapped and attacking).
   - Invocation's trigger creates a 4/4 white Angel token with flying (tapped and attacking).
5. **Activate Pathmaker Initiate** ({T}): target Ragavan (power 2) — Ragavan can't be blocked this turn.
6. **Cast Consuming Fervor** (flash via Sigarda's Aid) on the Angel token — it becomes 7/7.
7. **Declare blockers / combat damage:** The opponent's only remaining blockers are the two Labyrinth Guardians (2/3). They cannot block the Angel (flying, no opposing fliers remain) and cannot block Ragavan (unblockable). Their only options with two ground creatures:
   - **Both Guardians block Kari Zev** (menace allows exactly this): then Ragavan (2), Pathmaker (2), and the Angel (7) all get through — **11 damage**.
   - **One or both Guardians block Pathmaker Initiate** (or do nothing): then fewer than two creatures block Kari Zev, so menace makes Kari unblocked — Kari (2) + Ragavan (2) + Angel (7) — **11 damage**.
   - They cannot block Ragavan or the Angel at all, and can never cover both Kari (needs 2 blockers) and Pathmaker (needs 1) with only two creatures.

Either way, at least 11 damage is dealt — Angel 7 + Ragavan 2 + (Kari or Pathmaker) 2 ≥ 10. The opponent goes from 10 to 0 or less this combat, and you win the game.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

<solution>

2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

**Analysis of the puzzle:**
- Opponent: 10 life; blockers are Shimmerscale Drake (3/4 flying) and two Labyrinth Guardians (2/3).
- Labyrinth Guardians die when targeted by *any* spell (including my Auras/instants).
- Pathmaker Initiate makes a power-≤2 creature unblockable; Kari Zev has menace and creates Ragavan when attacking.
- Sigarda's Aid lets me cast Consuming Fervor, Invocation of Saint Traft, and True-Faith Censer at instant speed.
- The "Plains on top" note enables cycling Djeru's Resolve ({2}) to draw and play an extra land.

The key structure: bounce the Drake (only flyer that can block the Angel), make the Angel huge with Consuming Fervor, make Ragavan unblockable with Pathmaker, and Kari's menace means the two Guardians cannot profitably stop everything — blocking Kari requires committing *both* Guardians, which leaves Pathmaker through; chumping Pathmaker leaves Kari (menace) unblocked.

<solution>
1. **Cycle Djeru's Resolve** (pay {2}): discard it, draw the Plains (the known top card), and play the Plains as your land drop.
2. **Cast Disperse** targeting Shimmerscale Drake — the Drake returns to your opponent's hand. (Opponent has no mana to recast it.) Now no remaining blocker can block a flying creature.
3. **Cast Invocation of Saint Traft** on Kari Zev.
4. **Declare attackers:** Kari Zev and Pathmaker Initiate. Two triggers resolve:
   - Kari Zev's trigger creates Ragavan (2/1, tapped and attacking).
   - Invocation's trigger creates a 4/4 white Angel token with flying (tapped and attacking).
5. **Activate Pathmaker Initiate** ({T}): target Ragavan (power 2) — Ragavan can't be blocked this turn.
6. **Cast Consuming Fervor** (flash via Sigarda's Aid) on the Angel token — it becomes 7/7.
7. **Declare blockers / combat damage:** The opponent's only remaining blockers are the two Labyrinth Guardians (2/3). They cannot block the Angel (flying, no opposing fliers remain) and cannot block Ragavan (unblockable). Their only options with two ground creatures:
   - **Both Guardians block Kari Zev** (menace allows exactly this): then Ragavan (2), Pathmaker (2), and the Angel (7) all get through — **11 damage**.
   - **One or both Guardians block Pathmaker Initiate** (or do nothing): then fewer than two creatures block Kari Zev, so menace makes Kari unblocked — Kari (2) + Ragavan (2) + Angel (7) — **11 damage**.
   - They cannot block Ragavan or the Angel at all, and can never cover both Kari (needs 2 blockers) and Pathmaker (needs 1) with only two creatures.

Either way, at least 11 damage is dealt — Angel 7 + Ragavan 2 + (Kari or Pathmaker) 2 ≥ 10. The opponent goes from 10 to 0 or less this combat, and you win the game.
</solution>

4. **Declare attackers:** Kari Zev and Pathmaker Initiate. Two triggers resolve:
   - Kari Zev's trigger creates Ragavan (2/1, tapped and attacking).
   - Invocation's trigger creates a 4/4 white Angel token with flying (tapped and attacking).
5. **Activate Pathmaker Initiate** ({T}): target Ragavan (power 2) — Ragavan can't be blocked this turn.
6. **Cast Consuming Fervor** (flash via Sigarda's Aid) on the Angel token — it becomes 7/7.
7. **Declare blockers / combat damage:** The opponent's only remaining blockers are the two Labyrinth Guardians (2/3). They cannot block the Angel (flying, no opposing fliers remain) and cannot block Ragavan (unblockable). Their only options with two ground creatures:
   - **Both Guardians block Kari Zev** (menace allows exactly this): then Ragavan (2), Pathmaker (2), and the Angel (7) all get through — **11 damage**.
   - **One or both Guardians block Pathmaker Initiate** (or do nothing): then fewer than two creatures block Kari Zev, so menace makes Kari unblocked — Kari (2) + Ragavan (2) + Angel (7) — **11 damage**.
   - They cannot block Ragavan or the Angel at all, and can never cover both Kari (needs 2 blockers) and Pathmaker (needs 1) with only two creatures.

Either way, at least 11 damage is dealt — Angel 7 + Ragavan 2 + (Kari or Pathmaker) 2 ≥ 10. The opponent goes from 10 to 0 or less this combat, and you win the game.
